senses.gloss: (b. h.; v. preced.) [to let hang over,] to wrap one’s self up, to put on an upper garment.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 3:8:2">Y. Ned. III, 38ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>עתיד … לַעֲטוֹף טליתו וכ׳</he> wicked Esau (Rome) shall put on his cloak (for prayer, v. <cite ref="I00504"><he>טַלִּית</he></cite>) and sit down among the righteous &c.—Part. pass. <cite ref="P00438"><he>עָטוּף</he></cite>; pl. <he>עֲטוּפִים</he>, <cite ref="E00313"><he>עֲטוּפִין</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 20:3">Num. R. s. 20</cite> <he>נראין ע׳ לשלום</he> they appeared cloaked for peace, opp. <he>מזויינין למלחמה</he> in armor for war.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 1:9:4">Y. Ab. Zar. I, 40ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>ע׳ ויושבין</he> wrapped (in the judge’s cloak) and seated.
<cite ref="Shabbat 10a:4">Sabb. 10ᵃ</cite> <he>משיִתְעַטְּפוּ הדיינין</he> when the judges put their cloaks on.
<cite ref="Shabbat 31a">Ib. 31ᵃ</cite> <he>נ׳ ויצא וכ׳</he> he (Hillel) wrapped himself up and came out to meet him.
<cite ref="Ketubot 66b:11">Keth. 66ᵇ</cite> <he>נִתְעַטְּפָה בשערה</he> she covered herself with her hair.
<cite ref="Berakhot 16b:19">Ber. 16ᵇ</cite> <he>ותִתְעַטֵּף בחסידותיך</he> clothe thyself in thy kindness; a. fr.
